title: MultiLoReFT: Decoupling Shared and Modality-Specific Subspaces in Multimodal Learning via Low-Rank Representation Fine-Tuning
claim: Frozen unimodal representations are projected into shared and modality-specific low-rank subspaces, edited, and projected back, cleanly separating the two kinds of information.
layout: 2 panels, bottom-to-top flow on left, small decoupling schematic on right
description: The large left panel is a bottom-to-top diagram. Two frozen encoders (marked with snowflakes) at the bottom emit representations h1 (orange) and h2 (green). These feed pink low-rank projection blocks (R_m1, R_s, R_m2) and blue nonlinear transform blocks (f_m1, f_s1, f_s2, f_m2). The results land on grey parallelogram subspaces labeled modality 1 unique, shared, and modality 2 unique. Circled minus nodes subtract the edit from the projection. Transposed projections R^T map the result back up to circled plus nodes, which produce the fine-tuned representations Φ1 and Φ2 in a dashed box. A formula for Φ2 sits at the top right. The right panel is a small schematic. Φ1 and Φ2 pass through R_m1, R_s and R_m2 to give z_m1, z_s and z_m2. A legend at the bottom explains addition, subtraction and frozen parameters. Orange marks modality 1 and green marks modality 2.
caption: Overview of MultiLoReFT. Pretrained unimodal encoders (with frozen parameters) produce representations $h_1$ and $h_2$, which are fine-tuned through low-rank projections into shared ($R_s$) and modality-specific ($R_{m1}, R_{m2}$) subspaces. Nonlinear transforms ($f_{s1}, f_{s2}, f_{m1}, f_{m2}$) learn the representation edit in the lower-rank space that needs to be subtracted from the projection of the representations. Once edited in the low-rank space, the representations are projected back to form the fine-tuned representations $\Phi_1$ and $\Phi_2$. The right panel illustrates the decoupling of information into shared ($z_s$) and modality-unique ($z_{m1}, z_{m2}$) components. $z_s$ is computed as the mean of the shared projections across available modalities, using both when present and a single projection when only one is available.
abstract: Real-world perception and decision making are inherently multimodal, integrating complementary signals across modalities. However, training multimodal models faces two main obstacles. First, collecting large-scale, well-aligned paired multimodal datasets is often impractical, making end-to-end multimodal training difficult. Second, existing multimodal representations frequently entangle information shared across modalities with modality-specific information, hindering interpretability and control. We introduce MultiLoReFT, an efficient and scalable low-rank representation fine-tuning framework for multimodal learning with pretrained unimodal models. MultiLoReFT extends low-rank adaptation to the multimodal setting and learns interpretable projection subspaces that decouple shared and modality-specific information. Across simulated and real-world benchmarks, it produces representations that support multimodal prediction while explicitly revealing how shared and modality-specific information is distributed across modalities.
